components.css: :host{--yellow:#FFE14D;--yellow-ink:#2A2100;--soft:#C3D0FF;--line:rgba(255,255,255,.14);--panel:rgba(4,12,52,.62);--display:"Anton","Arial Narrow",sans-serif;--ui:"Barlow SC","Barlow Semi Condensed","Segoe UI",sans-serif;}.ds-i{width:20px;height:20px;flex:none;stroke:currentColor;fill:none;stroke-width:2;stroke-linecap:round;stroke-linejoin:round;}.ds-item{position:relative;width:150px;aspect-ratio:3/4;border-radius:5px;overflow:hidden;border:0;padding:0;text-align:left;box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 2px rgba(255,255,255,.25);transition:transform .15s;cursor:pointer;}.ds-item:hover{transform:translateY(-2px);}.ds-item:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--yellow);outline-offset:2px;}.ds-item::before{content:"";position:absolute;inset:0;background:radial-gradient(circle at 50% 35%,rgba(255,255,255,.35),transparent 60%);}.ds-item.legendary{background:linear-gradient(160deg,#FFB24A,#C14F14);}.ds-item.rare{background:linear-gradient(160deg,#4FC8FF,#1660B2);}.ds-art{position:absolute;left:50%;top:37%;width:54px;height:54px;margin:-27px 0 0 -27px;color:rgba(255,255,255,.75);stroke-width:1.6;}.ds-item.got .ds-art{opacity:.55;}.ds-band{position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;padding:8px 10px 9px;background:linear-gradient(0deg,rgba(0,0,20,.85),rgba(0,0,20,.55));}.ds-nm{display:block;font:400 15px/1.1 var(--display);text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.02em;color:#fff;transform:skewX(-7deg);transform-origin:0 100%;}.ds-tp{display:block;font:700 11px/1.2 var(--ui);text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.06em;color:rgba(255,255,255,.7);margin-top:3px;}.ds-own{position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:4px;padding:4px 7px;border-radius:3px;background:var(--yellow);color:var(--yellow-ink);font:700 11px/1 var(--ui);text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.05em;z-index:1;}.ds-own .ds-i{width:13px;height:13px;stroke-width:3;}

narrative.overview:
The app is a room the player already knows: the saturated blue Fortnite lobby, its heavy condensed caps leaning forward, its item shop of rarity-framed tiles with a refresh timer. A player who Alt+Tabs in mid-session should find the chest count, the next Treasure Hour, the missing prizes and the token odds without reading, because every element sits where the game taught them to look. The world is loud in colour and type but sparse in words: big numerals, short Portuguese labels, drawn line icons, bars instead of sentences.

Density is "one glance": the main view fits a short desktop window without scrolling, and secondary views (Prêmios, Agenda, Conta) only extend what the lobby already shows. Depth comes from a glowing radial field with diagonal light streaks behind translucent navy glass panels; colour is reserved. Yellow means "act" or "live". Rarity gradients belong only to item tiles. Everything else is blue, white and soft periwinkle.

It rejects the grey, dark-card admin dashboard of the first version: no neutral greys as surfaces, no small centred text blocks, no walls of times and names.
keyCharacteristics: Lobby-blue radial field with faint 115° light streaks, fixed behind everything.
Anton caps, skewed forward (about -7° to -8°), for every number, title, tab and button.
Parallelogram controls: tabs, buttons, the mark badge and step numbers are skewed boxes with upright contents.
One yellow, used for the primary action, the active tab, focus and anything live.
Rarity gradients on item tiles only; the prize row is the signature.
One-stroke drawn line icons (2px stroke, round caps) beside nearly every heading and label.

rules.name: The One Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yellow means "press this" or "this is happening now". A screen has one yellow button; any other yellow must be a live state, the active tab or an owned stamp.

rules.name: The Rarity Belongs to Items Rule
rules.body: Rarity gradients fill item tiles, the token medallion and event-type icons only. Panels, buttons and backgrounds never take a rarity colour.

rules.name: The No Grey Rule
rules.body: There are no neutral grey surfaces. Every dark surface is a translucent navy over the blue field.

rules.name: The Leaning Caps Rule
rules.body: Every Anton element that reads as a header or number is skewed forward (skewX -7°, origin bottom left). Anton has no italic; the skew is the italic. Body text never leans.

rules.name: The Numbers Shout Rule
rules.body: The answer is the biggest thing in its panel. A count, countdown or percentage is set in Anton at numeral size or larger, with its label in small Barlow caps underneath or beside it.

rules.name: The Glow Behind Rule
rules.body: Light comes from the field, not from the panels. Panels stay translucent so the radial and its streaks read through them; never make a panel opaque.

dos: Do set every number that answers a question in Anton, skewed -7°, at 34px or larger, with tabular figures.
Do pair each heading, tab, chip and stat label with a one-stroke line icon (24px grid, 2px stroke, round caps and joins).
Do keep yellow for the single primary action, the active tab, focus, owned stamps and live states, always with Yellow Ink text.
Do show prizes as rarity-gradient 3:4 tiles with art, a dark name band and an owned stamp.
Do keep panels translucent navy (62%) with a 1px 14% white hairline so the lobby field glows through.
Do make every control a skewed parallelogram (-8°) with upright contents and 3px corners.
Do keep the Painel's four answers visible without scrolling down to a 760px-tall window.
donts: Don't use neutral grey surfaces or opaque dark cards; that is the v0.1 dashboard this world replaced.
Don't put rarity gradients on panels, buttons or backgrounds.
Don't set white text on yellow, or add a second yellow button to a view.
Don't skew body text or chips; only Anton headers, numerals and controls lean.
Don't explain in sentences what a bar, icon or state can show.
Don't load fonts or icons from a CDN; fonts ship as local woff2 and icons as inline SVG symbols.
